keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1860-1884: Mirambo's state. The page says 'The 1860s saw Mirambo extend his domains westward and conquer several of the Nyamwezi chiefdoms' and gives no area; 'By the early 1880s this military organization had about 10,000 members'. The 90 km radius at the town of Urambo is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 1860: Mirambo's reign begins. 'nyamwezi king, from 1860 to 1884' (infobox 'Reign: 1860-1884'); the Nyamwezi page lists Urambo among the early-1800s Nyamwezi kingdoms. The page gives no founding of the state beyond his reign.

ledger.note: 1860s: Mirambo conquers Nyamwezi chiefdoms to the west. 'The 1860s saw Mirambo extend his domains westward and conquer several of the Nyamwezi chiefdoms'. 1865 is the middle of the decade, a placeholder; the page names no chiefdom.

ledger.note: 1871: war with Unyanyembe. 'In 1871 Unyanyembe was involved in another war, this time against Urambo'; in 1873 'the Urambo forces blockaded the ivory trade from Tabora'; in the 1870s Mirambo 'allied himself closely with Philippe Broyon, a Swiss merchant'.

ledger.note: 1884: the war ends with Mirambo's death. 'The war lasted until Mirambo's death in 1884.'

ledger.note: 1884: Mirambo dies and his state is no more on the map. 'Died: 1884'; 'Near the end of his life he grew ill, and died at the age 44.' The page is silent on what became of Urambo; the Nyamwezi page has the Germans 'pacifying' Unyamwezi in 1893.

sources.title: Mirambo

sources.title: Nyamwezi people
sources.note: Early-1800s Nyamwezi kingdoms (Unyanyembe, Ulyankhulu, Urambo); Unyanyembe 1858, 1860, 1871-1884 war with Urambo; German campaigns 1890-1893, Isike's death 1893.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Urambo row). Pages: Mirambo and Nyamwezi people. The Mirambo page is thin: no Uyowa, no war dates, no founding of the town of Urambo, no Ugowe, Ukonongo, Ujiji, Uvinza or Katanga trade route, no treaties with the Arabs or Europeans, no month for his death, nothing on his successor (Mpandashalo) or on German rule. The end year 1884 rests on his death; whether the state survived him is unrecorded (confidence 1).

Counterparts needing dossiers: unyanyembe (this batch), the Nyamwezi chiefdoms Mirambo conquered (none).
